PC: Determines mechanism of injury/nature of illness
Develops a General Impression of Patient
Vital Signs  HR, RR, SpO2, B/P, Temp
SAMPLE – Signs and Symptoms, Allergies, Medication, Pertinent Past History, Last Oral Intake, and Events Leading Up To Arrival
Assesses Onset, Provocation, Quality, Radiation, Severity, Time
Assess patient’s airway, breathing, and circulation
Apply a carbon monoxide monitor (if available)
Intubate the patient to maintain the airway
Implement a 500 ml normal saline bolus
MK: Identification of burns (rule of 9’s, superficial 🡪 full thickness)
Intubation versus immediate transport (with a potential airway burn the importance of securing an airway).
SBP: Identification of local burn centers and location.
